decision.expected_measurable_effect: On a complete re-run with terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.01 and holding_tip_speed_weight 0.1 (all other fields fixed): (1) Reach — expect reach_passed to stay true with terminal_error_m still at or below the 0.01 m tolerance; a terminal_error_m above tolerance would indicate over-braking. (2) Holding position — expect the final-window error_m maximum (0.0581381 m baseline) to fall toward the 0.01 m position limit as overshoot and residual oscillation shrink. (3) Holding speed — the primary target: expect the final-window speed range (0.6351726–1.5810153 m/s baseline) to fall toward the 0.02 m/s limit, with holding_speed_passed flipping to true; if speed drops but that criterion still misses, the change is insufficient. (4) Computation — expect no improvement and possibly slightly more solver work and wall time per update (baseline mean_update_s 17.2633 s against control_period_s 0.01 s, f9a95df66c188, f7ab6d4ba8e86, over update_count 35, fc346e9d815b6) because added cost terms can add iterations; this bounded weight experiment is not expected to fix deadline misses. Possible adverse effects: over-braking that lengthens the approach and raises terminal error or earlier-profile error, and extra solver cost. Observations that would weaken the hypothesis: holding speed falls toward 0.02 m/s while holding position error stays above 0.01 m; reach begins to fail; mean update time worsens while final-window speeds are unchanged; or the local comparison at the selected saved update shows no change in the predicted endpoint speed for the changed holding weight.
decision.rationale: Accepted diagnosis (report 36ce3d65…78c) records three distinct criteria over the same single run: reach_passed true with terminal_error_m 0.0076426 m below reach_tolerance_m 0.01 m (f8d67f9e274d5, fcb979e866da6, fa647af5bb139), while holding_position_passed (f8d748c8f831a) and holding_speed_passed (fa1daa92aa2a8) are both false: over the six selected final-window rows (row_count 6, coverage "all recorded samples in final holding window", fecdfb8087195, ffc94495c3135) error_m reaches 0.0581381 m (fcb0e9b40d6f4) against position_limit_m 0.01 m (f9645f047c162) and speed_m_s spans 0.6351726–1.5810153 m/s (fe0e01ea28ce0, fda80c000cd60) against speed_limit_m_s 0.02 m/s (ffb1646ded597); terminal_speed_m_s is still 0.6351726 m/s (f98954e7ddf8b). Hypothesis: the configured cost carries no tip-speed penalty at either node set — terminal_tip_speed_weight and holding_tip_speed_weight are both recorded 0.0 (f9662abf5728d, f942f13d7ee66), and the only speed-like legacy terms are small velocity weights (velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001, f91bc4fbc0fdd, ffa33d1ecc95e) against terminal_weight 5.0 (ff72488b0a318) — so nothing in the cost asks the tip to shed speed, which is consistent with (though not proof of) the recorded arrival-and-hold motion being dominated by residual tip speed inside the settling window rather than by position tracking. If that relevance is real, an explicit scaled squared tip-speed penalty at the terminal node and an integration-step-weighted tip-speed penalty at the scheduled holding nodes should brake the tip before and through the window; both weights are inside the granted editable scope and the settling settings required by the holding term are explicit (window_s 0.05 s, fce125aaa9bab; tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02 m/s, fc5e06377f30a). Values are a first bounded step, not a developer-prescribed choice and not a sweep: 0.01 for the dimensionless terminal term and 0.1 for the per-second holding term, the larger holding coefficient chosen because the holding cost is integration-step weighted across the short settling window whereas the terminal cost is a single dimensionless penalty on the horizon endpoint (the per-second weighting convention is why the two coefficients differ; no numeric equivalence is claimed). This record only states an improvement intent; nothing is built, simulated or scored by this decision, and no causal or dominance claim is made from this single execution (f836338b710d8). The requested paired local comparison uses the only saved update I observed whose effective plan horizon equals one control interval (update_id 34, effective_horizon 1 at t = 0.34 s, f838ec81fe684, f7fc929c609f0); it is a one-step projected-GVS check and may be insensitive to the integration-step-weighted holding term, so an unavailable or inconclusive result would not argue against the complete experiment.
